source.name: CDFW Upland Game hunt zones (services2.arcgis.com Upland_Game_AGOL_gdb FeatureServer layer 1, "zones_seasons")
source.boundary_caveat: Zone boundaries are CDFW's own published approximation, generalized to about 50 metres for display. They are for finding your way to the right zone and for tapping, never for deciding a property line or a legal boundary — the boundary of record is the description in Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations.
source.seasons_caveat: This file carries boundaries and names only. No season, bag limit or possession limit is taken from this map layer: the layer is published on its own cadence and the dates it carries were out of date when it was read. Every date this app shows for these species comes from CDFW's Upland Game Birds regulation page, and for American crow from CDFW's 2026-2027 Waterfowl, Upland Game, and Lands Regulations booklet, p. 53.

properties.zone_description:
The following areas are closed to hunting of American Crow. All other areas are open:
1) Those portions of Trinity and Mendocino National Forests south of Highway 36
2) North and east of a line beginning at the mouth of the Eel River; south along the Eel River to the town of Alton; east on Highway 36 from the town of Alton to Highway 89 west of Chester; south and east on Highways 89 and 395 to Interstate 15 near Hesperia; south on Interstate 15 to Interstate 10; and east on Interstate 10 to the California-Arizona border.

Quail Zone 1 includes the counties of Alpine, Butte, Del Norte,  Glenn, Humboldt, Inyo, Lassen, Modoc, Mono, Plumas, Shasta, Sierra, Siskiyou, Tehama, Trinity, and those portions of Amador, Calaveras, El Dorado, Fresno, Madera, Mariposa, Nevada, Placer, Tuolumne, Tulare, and Yuba counties lying east of the western boundary of the national forests.
Zone Q2:  The coastal quail season (all species) hunting zone includes the counties of Marin, Napa, Solano, Sonoma, Lake, and Mendocino.
Zone Q3:  Quail Zone 3 includes the balance of the state not included in Zones 1 and 2.
